subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the conflicting fork PR that fixes both reported gaps, or split the compaction and isolated-cron repairs across separate same-repo PRs?
rationale: The source bug and likely fix shape are clear, but an exact closing fork PR exists and conflicts while a newer same-repo PR fixes only one half, so automation should not race maintainer ownership of the landing path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace The Full Fix
options.body: Refresh the fork work into a target-repo PR, or open a narrow replacement that fixes both isolated-cron matching and compaction counter preservation with regression tests.

options.title: Split The Repairs
options.body: Review the existing same-repo compaction PR as a partial fix, then keep this issue open for a separate isolated-cron matching PR.

options.title: Wait On The Fork
options.body: Leave this issue paired with the conflicting fork PR and wait for the contributor to refresh it before any target-repo replacement is opened.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace The Full Fix
recommendation.body: Refresh the fork work into a target-repo PR, or open a narrow replacement that fixes both isolated-cron matching and compaction counter preservation with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refactored the current reminder-guard path and are the strongest history-backed owner for choosing the landing shape.
